title: Revisiting the Equation-of-Motion Method: A Universal Framework for Correlated Quantum Systems
abstract: A general implementation of the equation-of-motion (EOM) formalism for correlated many-body states is presented and applied to the description of collective excitations in atomic nuclei. While EOM approaches are traditionally formulated on top of independent-particle reference states, the present work extends the method to correlated reference states generated by modern many-body solvers. This formulation enables a consistent treatment of ground-state correlations and excited-state dynamics within a unified framework. Particular emphasis is placed on collective nuclear excitations employing chiral nuclear Hamiltonians in an ab initio context. The approach is motivated by the renewed interest in EOM techniques across several fields, including quantum chemistry and quantum computing, where they provide efficient and systematically improvable descriptions of excitation spectra. The present results demonstrate that the EOM framework offers a flexible and powerful tool for the microscopic description of nuclear spectroscopy beyond the traditional mean-field paradigm.
summary: This paper introduces an advanced Equation-of-Motion (EOM) formalism designed to treat collective excitations in strongly correlated quantum systems, specifically atomic nuclei. By extending the method to use correlated ground states rather than simple mean-field approximations, it provides a unified and powerful tool for calculating excitation spectra beyond traditional limits. This advancement is significant for any field requiring accurate dynamics of complex many-body wavefunctions.
main_problem: The central problem is developing a universal, consistent framework for describing excited states and collective excitations in complex, correlated quantum many-body systems.
main_result: The authors present an extended Equation-of-Motion (EOM) formalism that successfully incorporates ground-state correlations by operating on correlated reference states, moving beyond traditional mean-field approximations.
method: The method involves deriving the EOM equations from the Time-Dependent Variational Principle and solving the resulting generalized eigenvalue problem, which yields normal modes of the energy function.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to atomic nuclei using chiral nuclear Hamiltonians in an ab initio context. The formalism itself is general for any correlated quantum system described by a Hamiltonian H.
key_observables: Excitation spectra, collective nuclear excitations (e.g., dipole polarizability), and spectroscopic properties beyond the mean-field limit.
important_parameters: The structure depends on the choice of reference state $|\Psiangle$ and the truncation level of the excitation operators used in the formalism.
main_assumptions: The primary extension is assuming that the EOM can be consistently formulated using correlated reference states, overcoming the limitation to independent-particle assumptions inherent in older methods.
figures_summary: Not specified by notes; the mathematical structure involves matrix equations (like Eq. 15) representing the generalized eigenvalue problem for excitation modes.
paper_structure: The paper develops the general EOM formalism from first principles using the TD variational principle, establishes its universal operator structure, and then applies it to specific physical systems like atomic nuclei, comparing results against established methods (RPA, CC).
why_interesting: While focused on nuclear physics, the core mathematical machinery—the generalized EOM framework for excited states built upon correlated reference states—is highly relevant to open quantum systems dynamics and time-dependent variational approaches in AMO physics.
